world.title: Ukraine says Starlink satellite limits persist as Trump vows intervention
world.summary: Ukrainian officials said Friday that speed restrictions continued to disrupt Starlink, SpaceX’s satellite internet network, and its military-grade service Starshield, despite President Donald Trump’s claim the day before that SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk had restored access. Trump said he had not spoken to Musk but
world.content: Ukrainian officials said Friday that speed restrictions continued to disrupt Starlink, SpaceX’s satellite internet network, and its military-grade service Starshield, despite President Donald Trump’s claim the day before that SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk had restored access. Trump said he had not spoken to Musk but would do so if problems remained. Ukrainian defense sources said connections continued to drop when drones reached about 161 km/h (100 mph). The restrictions affect both attack drones and interceptor drones used against Russian aerial attacks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told the Hudson Institute that the speed restrictions remained and that deliveries of previously agreed interceptors to defend against Russian ballistic missiles were also delayed. Tests by a Ukrainian drone unit found that some connections briefly worked at higher speeds but then dropped, returning only after the drones slowed. Trump said he would “get it straightened out” if service remained impaired but declined to say who imposed the limits. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham urged Trump in a call to ensure Ukraine had full access. Separately, Ukraine’s Defense Ministry signed a letter of intent with Finland’s ICEYE and Nokia to explore a satellite communications system under Ukrainian control.
world.image_alt: Ukraine says Starlink satellite limits persist as Trump vows intervention

world.title: Trump threatens renewed Iran strikes as envoy floats weekend attack
world.summary: U.S. Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack said Friday that a U.S. strike on Iran could come as soon as this weekend. President Donald Trump told reporters he knew nothing about such plans, then warned at a Florida rally that Washington could launch “another little Epic Fury” if Tehran did not agree to a deal. The White Hou
world.content: U.S. Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack said Friday that a U.S. strike on Iran could come as soon as this weekend. President Donald Trump told reporters he knew nothing about such plans, then warned at a Florida rally that Washington could launch “another little Epic Fury” if Tehran did not agree to a deal. The White House had said Thursday that attacks would not resume before the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, contradicting Barrack’s suggestion of imminent action. Barrack said Washington was not seeking to overthrow Iran’s government, in contrast to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has called toppling it the only way to remove the threat from Tehran. Netanyahu faces an Israeli election on Oct. 27. The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began with airstrikes on Feb. 28 and remains unresolved after months of stalled diplomacy; a ceasefire and memorandum of understanding were intended to lead to a final peace agreement. Barrack said negotiations were continuing, but Trump gave no timetable for a decision or details of the terms Iran would need to accept.
world.image_alt: Trump threatens renewed Iran strikes as envoy floats weekend attack

world.title: US warns Iran plots against Americans are advanced, cuts embassy staffing
world.summary: U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio in an Oct. 23 memo that Iran has “substantially increased” efforts to target U.S. personnel, with lethal plots at “advanced stages” in the Middle East and other countries. The one-page, unclassified memo does not name targets, spec
world.content: U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio in an Oct. 23 memo that Iran has “substantially increased” efforts to target U.S. personnel, with lethal plots at “advanced stages” in the Middle East and other countries. The one-page, unclassified memo does not name targets, specify locations beyond the Middle East or describe methods. Clayton said intelligence about the alleged plots should reach more U.S. personnel who may be at risk and offered to make as much of it as possible available at a lower classification level. The State Department ordered nonessential staff and family members to leave U.S. diplomatic posts in Saudi Arabia earlier this week, then reduced staffing at missions in the United Arab Emirates, Lebanon, Qatar and Jordan on Friday. A U.S. official cited both Iranian plots and the threat of attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. The Saudi measure was an ordered departure; the other changes were staffing reductions. President Donald Trump said Friday that Washington could launch another operation against Iran or reach a deal, as his administration weighs whether to resume military action. U.S. officials have not said whether the alleged plots are imminent. The U.S. midterm elections are scheduled for Nov. 3.
world.image_alt: US warns Iran plots against Americans are advanced, cuts embassy staffing

world.title: Typhoon Champi injures 527 in Taiwan, heads toward China
world.summary: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing one person and injuring 527 as it weakened and moved north toward China. The storm had earlier reached super-typhoon strength. The man was swept away by waves near Liuqiu, while strong winds and heavy rain brought down trees and cut electricity. Emergency crews had
world.content: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing one person and injuring 527 as it weakened and moved north toward China. The storm had earlier reached super-typhoon strength. The man was swept away by waves near Liuqiu, while strong winds and heavy rain brought down trees and cut electricity. Emergency crews had restored power to most affected households by Saturday but were still working to reconnect homes. The storm turned south near Taiwan’s northeastern Yilan coast before looping offshore and heading north. Gusts reached 227 kph in some coastal areas, and the storm was about 150 to 170 kilometers east or northeast of Taiwan on Saturday, according to varying updates from the island’s weather agency. Flight cancellations fell to 259 on Saturday from nearly 1,000 the previous day, but northern and central areas of Taiwan, including Taipei, kept schools and offices closed for a second day. China dispatched a team to Zhejiang and warned of strong winds and heavy rain through Sunday; Taiwan’s weather agency expected to lift its land warning by Saturday evening.
world.image_alt: Typhoon Champi injures 527 in Taiwan, heads toward China

world.title: Brazil
world.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro traded accusations in their final televised debate Friday, two days before a runoff that will decide whether Lula wins a fourth nonconsecutive term or Bolsonaro succeeds him. A Datafolha poll published Thursday showed the candidates tied at 50%
world.content: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro traded accusations in their final televised debate Friday, two days before a runoff that will decide whether Lula wins a fourth nonconsecutive term or Bolsonaro succeeds him. A Datafolha poll published Thursday showed the candidates tied at 50% of valid votes, after Bolsonaro led the Oct. 4 first round with 47.03% to Lula's 45.16%. The debate on TV Globo in Rio de Janeiro was more restrained than their earlier encounter but still featured sharp exchanges over living costs, crime, government spending and corruption allegations. Lula defended wage increases and public investment; Bolsonaro said prices and household debt were rising and criticized the government's spending and tax policies. The candidates are making their final campaign push Saturday, when Brazilian election law bars broadcast campaign advertising but permits rallies. Voters are scheduled to choose between them Sunday, Oct. 25.

world.title: Fire engulfs Nazi-era Eagle’s Nest retreat in Bavaria; suspect detained
world.summary: German police detained a suspect after a fire engulfed the Kehlsteinhaus, the Bavarian mountain site known as the Eagle’s Nest and once used by Adolf Hitler and Nazi officials. The blaze began Friday evening, Oct. 23, near Berchtesgaden. About 200 firefighters and emergency personnel were sent to the scene, and police
world.content: German police detained a suspect after a fire engulfed the Kehlsteinhaus, the Bavarian mountain site known as the Eagle’s Nest and once used by Adolf Hitler and Nazi officials. The blaze began Friday evening, Oct. 23, near Berchtesgaden. About 200 firefighters and emergency personnel were sent to the scene, and police said no one was found inside and no injuries were reported. The building was still burning early Saturday as crews struggled to reach the site, which stands 1,834 metres above sea level. Police said the fire’s cause was unknown and investigators were examining whether the detained person was connected to it. No motive had been announced. A smoke detector triggered the fire alarm, and firefighters found the building fully ablaze when they arrived. The state of Bavaria owns the Kehlsteinhaus, which has operated since 1952 as a restaurant and exhibition space documenting its Nazi-era history.
world.image_alt: Fire engulfs Nazi-era Eagle’s Nest retreat in Bavaria; suspect detained

world.title: Israeli election pits Netanyahu against Eisenkot as polls predict deadlock
world.summary: Israelis vote on Oct. 27 in a parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s current term, but final polls project neither his bloc nor the opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot will win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The vote is the first since th
world.content: Israelis vote on Oct. 27 in a parliamentary election that could end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s current term, but final polls project neither his bloc nor the opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot will win the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The vote is the first since the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023, and the wars that followed in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Netanyahu’s handling of the security failures and conflicts is central to the contest. Polls published before a campaign-period ban forecast 50 seats for Netanyahu’s governing camp and between 52 and 56 for the opposition bloc. Arab-led parties were projected to win 14 to 16 seats, potentially giving them leverage in coalition talks, although several opposition parties have ruled out joining a government with the Arab party Ra’am. Polling stations are due to close at 10 p.m. Tuesday, when exit polls are expected. If no coalition can be formed, repeat elections could be held in early 2027, with Netanyahu serving as caretaker prime minister.
world.image_alt: Israeli election pits Netanyahu against Eisenkot as polls predict deadlock

world.title: Macron calls Paris suburb shooting racist terrorism as prosecutors investigate
world.summary: A gunman killed one person and wounded five others, including a 12-year-old girl, in shootings across Trappes and La Verrière, west of Paris, on Friday. Police arrested the 39-year-old suspect in nearby Coignières less than 20 minutes after the shooting began, French officials said. French President Emmanuel Macron cal
world.content: A gunman killed one person and wounded five others, including a 12-year-old girl, in shootings across Trappes and La Verrière, west of Paris, on Friday. Police arrested the 39-year-old suspect in nearby Coignières less than 20 minutes after the shooting began, French officials said. French President Emmanuel Macron called the attack a “terrorist and racist” act, saying victims were targeted because of their skin colour or perceived religion. France’s National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor’s Office (PNAT) opened an investigation into murder linked to a terrorist enterprise. Investigators are examining whether victims were targeted because of their actual or perceived race, ethnicity, nationality or religion; the motive remains under investigation. The suspect’s car contained a Sten-type submachine gun and a tear-gas canister. Investigators found three gas cylinders and wires connected to a timer in his apartment. A close family member was also taken into custody. Investigators are examining possible terrorist conspiracy and possession of a Category A weapon.
world.image_alt: Macron calls Paris suburb shooting racist terrorism as prosecutors investigate

business.title: U.S. consumer sentiment nears record low as prices strain households
business.summary: U.S. consumer sentiment slipped to 48.0 in October, its second-lowest reading on record, as inflation and higher prices weighed on households ahead of the Nov. 3 congressional elections. The University of Michigan index stood at 48.1 in September and reached a record low of 44.8 in May, shortly after the Iran war began
business.content: U.S. consumer sentiment slipped to 48.0 in October, its second-lowest reading on record, as inflation and higher prices weighed on households ahead of the Nov. 3 congressional elections. The University of Michigan index stood at 48.1 in September and reached a record low of 44.8 in May, shortly after the Iran war began. Joanne Hsu, director of the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers, said sentiment was 10% below a year earlier and 15% below February, before the conflict. Consumers expected inflation of 4.7% over the next year, up from 4.6% in September; five-year expectations reached 3.5%. Rising fuel costs and affordability were prominent consumer concerns, and the survey found that sentiment deteriorated mainly among independents. Federal Reserve officials are due to meet next week and are widely expected to hold their benchmark rate at 3.75%-4.00% after raising it in September.
business.image_alt: U.S. consumer sentiment nears record low as prices strain households

business.title: Oncologists endorse Moderna melanoma vaccine as long-term evidence remains pending
business.summary: Oncologists described Moderna and Merck’s individualized melanoma vaccine as a clinically important advance after trial results showed it helped prevent the cancer from returning after surgery when paired with Keytruda, Merck’s immunotherapy. The approach uses each patient’s tumor mutations to tailor an mRNA vaccine, a
business.content: Oncologists described Moderna and Merck’s individualized melanoma vaccine as a clinically important advance after trial results showed it helped prevent the cancer from returning after surgery when paired with Keytruda, Merck’s immunotherapy. The approach uses each patient’s tumor mutations to tailor an mRNA vaccine, and specialists told CNBC it could help prevent cancer from spreading after surgery. Researchers followed the trial’s 1,137 participants for about 25 months and will continue tracking them to assess overall survival and how long the benefit lasts. The results are due for presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting in Madrid on Saturday, Oct. 24, while Moderna and Merck are discussing regulatory steps. Analysts have questioned whether the treatment’s commercial potential can justify its complex, patient-specific manufacturing process.
business.image_alt: Oncologists endorse Moderna melanoma vaccine as long-term evidence remains pending

business.title: US activity grows in October as business prices hit four-year high
business.summary: U.S. private-sector activity continued to expand in October. The S&P Global flash composite output index eased to 57.6 from 58.4 in September but remained near a multi-year high; readings above 50 indicate growth. The survey’s output-price gauge rose to 59.8, its highest since August 2022, as strong demand and worsenin
business.content: U.S. private-sector activity continued to expand in October. The S&P Global flash composite output index eased to 57.6 from 58.4 in September but remained near a multi-year high; readings above 50 indicate growth. The survey’s output-price gauge rose to 59.8, its highest since August 2022, as strong demand and worsening supply delays allowed businesses to pass on higher costs. Economists expect the government’s advance estimate of gross domestic product next week to show about 3% annualized growth in the July-September quarter. The Federal Reserve is expected to hold rates at its meeting next week and could raise them again in December. Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said rising costs, supply bottlenecks and growing backlogs were making it easier for companies to raise prices.
business.image_alt: US activity grows in October as business prices hit four-year high

business.title: American Express cuts 5% of workforce as it prepares for AI
business.summary: American Express said on Oct. 23 it will cut about 5% of its global workforce, or roughly 3,800 jobs, as it reorganizes to simplify operations and prepare more processes for automation using artificial intelligence. The company recorded a $336 million restructuring charge in the third quarter; it had about 76,800 emplo
business.content: American Express said on Oct. 23 it will cut about 5% of its global workforce, or roughly 3,800 jobs, as it reorganizes to simplify operations and prepare more processes for automation using artificial intelligence. The company recorded a $336 million restructuring charge in the third quarter; it had about 76,800 employees at the end of 2025. Third-quarter revenue rose 9% to $20.06 billion, slightly below analysts’ forecast, while net income increased 28% to $3.71 billion. Adjusted earnings of $4.68 a share topped estimates, and American Express raised its full-year earnings-per-share outlook to $18.30-$18.60 from $17.30-$17.90. Executives have not specified which teams or locations will be affected.
business.image_alt: American Express cuts 5% of workforce as it prepares for AI

business.title: Volvo cuts 2,500 jobs after quarterly loss as China sales slump
business.summary: Volvo Cars will cut 2,500 jobs worldwide and save an additional 5 billion kronor ($503 million) after the Swedish automaker swung from a year-earlier profit to a third-quarter net loss of 5.7 billion kronor. Revenue fell 23% to 66.9 billion kronor as intense competition in China, U.S. tariffs and the removal of U.S. el
business.content: Volvo Cars will cut 2,500 jobs worldwide and save an additional 5 billion kronor ($503 million) after the Swedish automaker swung from a year-earlier profit to a third-quarter net loss of 5.7 billion kronor. Revenue fell 23% to 66.9 billion kronor as intense competition in China, U.S. tariffs and the removal of U.S. electric-vehicle incentives weighed on sales and margins. About 2,000 of the positions are in Sweden. The company said it would end consultant contracts and use natural attrition and targeted exit packages to reduce its workforce. It expects the full financial benefit of the cost measures by the end of 2027. Volvo has already withdrawn its full-year sales and cash-flow guidance. Chief Executive Håkan Samuelsson said it was too early to rule out further cost cuts if the turnaround plan falls short.
business.image_alt: Volvo cuts 2,500 jobs after quarterly loss as China sales slump

business.title: AI-assisted discovery of PHP flaws raises concerns about defenses
business.summary: Cybersecurity executives and researchers warned that AI-assisted discovery and exploitation of software flaws could outpace organizations’ ability to secure their systems, as businesses continue patching two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language used by an estimated 70% of websites. The bugs could l
business.content: Cybersecurity executives and researchers warned that AI-assisted discovery and exploitation of software flaws could outpace organizations’ ability to secure their systems, as businesses continue patching two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language used by an estimated 70% of websites. The bugs could let attackers take control of vulnerable web servers and steal data, but the BBC said no successful exploits had been reported as of Friday. Researchers at the firms Wiz and Calif used AI tools to uncover the flaws, which had gone undetected for years. The discoveries have renewed concerns that attackers could use similar tools to turn newly disclosed weaknesses into working exploits more quickly. Cloudflare and Amazon reported a sharp rise in attempted attacks after the vulnerabilities became public, while organizations took some services offline as a precaution. The PHP Foundation released fixes on Oct. 21, but applying them across websites, plugins, frameworks and hosting services takes time. Security leaders say smaller organizations face particular difficulty and urge companies to strengthen basic defenses, identify the software they rely on and patch exposed systems promptly.
business.image_alt: AI-assisted discovery of PHP flaws raises concerns about defenses

business.title: AI infrastructure sell-off deepens as credit strains threaten spending
business.summary: Shares in AI infrastructure companies fell sharply this week as investors questioned whether returns will justify heavy borrowing and data-center spending. AI infrastructure company CoreWeave’s credit-default-swap spreads rose above 11%, while yields on its 2031 and 2032 unsecured bonds topped 15%. SK Hynix also droppe
business.content: Shares in AI infrastructure companies fell sharply this week as investors questioned whether returns will justify heavy borrowing and data-center spending. AI infrastructure company CoreWeave’s credit-default-swap spreads rose above 11%, while yields on its 2031 and 2032 unsecured bonds topped 15%. SK Hynix also dropped plans for a U.S. listing of its Solidigm storage unit, citing market conditions. Meta reported negative free cash flow of more than $2 billion in the third quarter and raised its 2026 capital-spending floor to $135 billion, while credit-risk measures for Meta, Nvidia and Oracle hit records. Higher financing costs and doubts about whether AI revenue and earnings will justify spending have contributed to the retreat. Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang defended demand for neocloud services, while analysts warned that weaker funding could hurt firms with large debt burdens. Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon are due to report earnings next week.
business.image_alt: AI infrastructure sell-off deepens as credit strains threaten spending

business.title: Brent settles at $116.72 as Gulf attacks raise supply fears
business.summary: Brent crude settled at $116.72 a barrel on Friday, Oct. 23, its highest close since April 29, after briefly topping $117 as investors priced in the risk of renewed U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran and further attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure. U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate rose 3.8% to $103.27. Brent gaine
business.content: Brent crude settled at $116.72 a barrel on Friday, Oct. 23, its highest close since April 29, after briefly topping $117 as investors priced in the risk of renewed U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran and further attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure. U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate rose 3.8% to $103.27. Brent gained 6.2% over the week, its third consecutive weekly advance. The rise followed Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, reports of Iranian strikes on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz and threats by Tehran to target Gulf energy assets if a new offensive begins. Although some estimates show crude exports through Hormuz have recovered to near or above prewar levels, traders remain concerned that infrastructure damage and shipping constraints could disrupt supply. The U.S. midterm elections are scheduled for Nov. 3, and analysts cited by the Financial Times and MarketWatch expect escalation risks to remain a market concern after the vote. White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly told MarketWatch the United States would not attack Iran before the elections. President Donald Trump said Friday the war could end quickly, while also saying the U.S. was taking the oil it wanted.
business.image_alt: Brent settles at $116.72 as Gulf attacks raise supply fears

science.title: Tailored mRNA vaccine cuts melanoma relapse risk; durability remains unknown
science.summary: An international phase 3 trial found that adding an individualized mRNA vaccine to standard pembrolizumab treatment reduced the two-year risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42% in patients whose high-risk tumors had been surgically removed. The study enrolled 1,137 patients; 82% of those receiving the combination w
science.content: An international phase 3 trial found that adding an individualized mRNA vaccine to standard pembrolizumab treatment reduced the two-year risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42% in patients whose high-risk tumors had been surgically removed. The study enrolled 1,137 patients; 82% of those receiving the combination were alive without recurrence at two years, compared with 70% of those given pembrolizumab alone. The vaccine, intismeran, is designed from mutations in each patient’s tumor to help the immune system identify cancer cells. Researchers continue to follow participants because the current data do not establish whether the treatment improves long-term survival or how long its benefit lasts. The results are scheduled for presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology congress in Madrid on Oct. 24.
science.image_alt: Tailored mRNA vaccine cuts melanoma relapse risk; durability remains unknown

science.title: Study estimates U.S. drinking water PFAS levels are undercounted by half
science.summary: A study of federal monitoring data estimates that conventional reporting captures only 44% of the average concentration of 25 types of PFAS in U.S. community water systems because results below laboratory reporting limits are often counted as zero. Researchers analyzed about 1.86 million test results from 9,991 systems
science.content: A study of federal monitoring data estimates that conventional reporting captures only 44% of the average concentration of 25 types of PFAS in U.S. community water systems because results below laboratory reporting limits are often counted as zero. Researchers analyzed about 1.86 million test results from 9,991 systems; 98% of the results were below those limits. The estimates come from statistical models, not measurements of concentrations below reporting limits, and the study did not determine whether water was unsafe or how much PFAS people consumed. Lead author Gehendra Kharel said he plans to repeat the analysis using newer Environmental Protection Agency data and called for clearer reporting and further testing where feasible.
science.image_alt: Study estimates U.S. drinking water PFAS levels are undercounted by half

science.title: Lab tests find magma can store extra oxygen under pressure
science.summary: Molten basalt can absorb more oxygen than its other elements would predict, with uptake increasing under pressure, researchers report in a study published in *National Science Review*. At 7 gigapascals, samples supplied with platinum oxide held more than 5% excess oxygen by weight; control samples held 0.2% to 0.5%. Th
science.content: Molten basalt can absorb more oxygen than its other elements would predict, with uptake increasing under pressure, researchers report in a study published in *National Science Review*. At 7 gigapascals, samples supplied with platinum oxide held more than 5% excess oxygen by weight; control samples held 0.2% to 0.5%. The researchers propose that magma could release some of this stored oxygen as it rises and pressure falls, potentially contributing to increases in atmospheric oxygen 2.5 billion to 2 billion years ago. They estimate that magma releasing excess oxygen equal to 0.27% of its weight could supply as much oxygen as today’s atmosphere contains.
science.image_alt: Lab tests find magma can store extra oxygen under pressure

science.title: MIT engineers build light-controlled swimming robot powered by living muscle
science.summary: Massachusetts Institute of Technology engineers built a paper-thin swimming robot powered by living muscle cells that contract in response to light, allowing researchers to steer it through water and a simple underwater maze. Its flexible gel frame carries two independently activated fins, which researchers control by
science.content: Massachusetts Institute of Technology engineers built a paper-thin swimming robot powered by living muscle cells that contract in response to light, allowing researchers to steer it through water and a simple underwater maze. Its flexible gel frame carries two independently activated fins, which researchers control by illuminating either side. The researchers said this was the first demonstration of a very thin, two-dimensional robot propelled by living muscle; earlier biohybrid designs generally used bulkier three-dimensional muscle structures made from millions of cells. The team says thinner designs could cost less to make and move more efficiently, but the work demonstrates a prototype rather than a practical deployment.
science.image_alt: MIT engineers build light-controlled swimming robot powered by living muscle

science.title: WMO says powerful El Niño likely to persist through February 2027
science.summary: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says the strong El Niño developing in the tropical Pacific is expected to peak in December and is nearly certain to persist until February 2027. The climate pattern, which warms the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is forecast to bring above-average temperatures across
science.content: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says the strong El Niño developing in the tropical Pacific is expected to peak in December and is nearly certain to persist until February 2027. The climate pattern, which warms the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is forecast to bring above-average temperatures across much of the world and shift rainfall patterns, increasing drought and flood risks in different regions. In Ecuador, the Navy’s Oceanographic and Antarctic Institute reported sea temperatures as much as 5.2°C above normal off Ecuador and Peru. It linked the unusually warm water to exceptional coastal rainfall, rainfall deficits in the Andean highlands and Amazon, and reduced nutrient levels affecting some fisheries. Officials urged preparations for coastal flooding. Separately, Copernicus reported that the global average sea-surface temperature outside polar regions reached a September record of 21.05°C.
science.image_alt: WMO says powerful El Niño likely to persist through February 2027

science.title: OpenAI publishes 722 AI-generated math manuscripts, prompting research debate
science.summary: OpenAI published 722 mathematical manuscripts generated by an advanced AI system in early October, weeks after announcing that AI agents had solved the Navier–Stokes problem, which describes fluid motion. Researchers have debated the reliability of the proofs, credit for the research and whether answers without clear e
science.content: OpenAI published 722 mathematical manuscripts generated by an advanced AI system in early October, weeks after announcing that AI agents had solved the Navier–Stokes problem, which describes fluid motion. Researchers have debated the reliability of the proofs, credit for the research and whether answers without clear explanations count as mathematical progress. Terence Tao, a mathematics professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, said companies had used open problems to evaluate AI models and released poorly polished results. Two researchers who had spent a year working on Navier–Stokes with OpenAI tools said the company used their work to develop its reasoning. Other mathematicians say AI can accelerate searches but stress the importance of selecting worthwhile questions and explaining proofs. Ken Duffy, a mathematics professor at Northeastern, said research depends on “finding a good question to ask”.
science.image_alt: OpenAI publishes 722 AI-generated math manuscripts, prompting research debate

science.title: European study links 32,619 summer heat deaths to climate change
science.summary: A Nature Health study published Friday estimates that heat killed 50,391 people in 854 European cities during summer 2026, including 32,619 deaths attributed to human-caused warming. The estimated toll is the highest in the study’s 2000–26 record, but the analysis covers cities representing about 40% of the population
science.content: A Nature Health study published Friday estimates that heat killed 50,391 people in 854 European cities during summer 2026, including 32,619 deaths attributed to human-caused warming. The estimated toll is the highest in the study’s 2000–26 record, but the analysis covers cities representing about 40% of the population in 30 countries and excludes a deadly May heatwave. The researchers also published a longer-term analysis of heat mortality through 2025. The summer 2026 estimate includes 833 deaths among people aged 20 to 44. The estimates come from models, not counts of individually confirmed deaths; heat is often omitted from death certificates. The European Commission is due to propose a climate-preparedness law on Tuesday and is preparing a heatwave plan that includes data gathering and early-warning systems.
science.image_alt: European study links 32,619 summer heat deaths to climate change

science.title: Tanker spill reaches UAE beaches, forcing closures and marine assessments
science.summary: The United Arab Emirates said on Friday, Oct. 23, that oil leaking from a tanker had reached beaches in Umm Al Quwain, prompting coastal closures and cleanup operations. Analysis of satellite images from Oct. 21 showed a slick about 40 kilometres long, covering roughly 190 square kilometres and extending to within six
science.content: The United Arab Emirates said on Friday, Oct. 23, that oil leaking from a tanker had reached beaches in Umm Al Quwain, prompting coastal closures and cleanup operations. Analysis of satellite images from Oct. 21 showed a slick about 40 kilometres long, covering roughly 190 square kilometres and extending to within six kilometres of shore. Video later showed oil washing onto beaches. Maritime intelligence firms and security sources identified the damaged vessel as the Panama-flagged tanker Gem No.2, which was struck by a projectile on Oct. 9. UAE authorities have not named the ship or said what caused the spill. The spill’s composition and full environmental effects remain uncertain: satellite imagery cannot establish whether it is crude oil or a thin, diluted sheen, and researchers say further assessment is needed. Authorities say containment operations, surveys and environmental assessments are continuing. Beaches will remain closed until technical teams determine safety measures.
science.image_alt: Tanker spill reaches UAE beaches, forcing closures and marine assessments

sports.title: Ferrari
sports.summary: Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc topped both Friday practice sessions for the United States Grand Prix in Austin, setting a fastest lap of 1:35.291 in the second session, just 0.042 seconds ahead of Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen was third, 0.189 seconds behind Leclerc, leaving Fe
sports.content: Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc topped both Friday practice sessions for the United States Grand Prix in Austin, setting a fastest lap of 1:35.291 in the second session, just 0.042 seconds ahead of Mercedes’ championship leader Kimi Antonelli. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen was third, 0.189 seconds behind Leclerc, leaving Ferrari, Mercedes and Red Bull closely matched ahead of Saturday’s qualifying at the Circuit of the Americas. Antonelli, 20, can clinch his first Formula One drivers’ title this weekend if he wins Sunday’s race, Mercedes teammate George Russell finishes ninth or lower and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton finishes fifth or lower. Antonelli leads Russell by 102 points, while Ferrari is seeking its first win since the British Grand Prix. Leclerc led both sessions on the first day of running with Ferrari’s revised car, but cautioned against reading too much into practice. Qualifying is scheduled for Saturday, October 24, after a final practice session, with the race on Sunday, October 25.

sports.content: Chicago opened NFL Week 7 with a 30-24 win over New England on Thursday. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye threw a 48-yard touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson in the final seconds of the first half, but the Bears held on to win. The result opened a 14-game schedule that also features the NFL’s first game in France, between Pittsburgh and New Orleans. Sunday’s schedule includes AFC North rivals Cincinnati and Baltimore, Green Bay against Detroit, and Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker III returning to Seattle, where he helped the Seahawks win the Super Bowl before joining the Chiefs. The week closes Monday night with Dallas visiting Philadelphia. The New York Giants will start J.J. McCarthy at quarterback against Houston after his 243-yard fourth-quarter appearance in Week 6. The remaining games are scheduled for Oct. 25-26.

sports.content: England led France 36-0 at halftime in their Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday, a game they needed to win to remain in contention for the semi-finals. England lost their opener 30-12 to Tonga, while Samoa beat Papua New Guinea 64-6, increasing the points-difference target for England. The tournament combines Pools B and C into a six-team table, with only the top two reaching the semi-finals. England need to turn their halftime lead into a large win and beat Papua New Guinea on Friday, 30 October; qualification also depends on results elsewhere and their points difference.

sports.summary: The 6-0 San Francisco 49ers ruled out wide receiver Mike Evans, defensive end Nick Bosa and receiver Deebo Samuel for Sunday’s game in Atlanta. sports.content: The 6-0 San Francisco 49ers ruled out wide receiver Mike Evans, defensive end Nick Bosa and receiver Deebo Samuel for Sunday’s game in Atlanta. Linebackers Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford and safety Marques Sigle are also out. Coach Kyle Shanahan said San Francisco may dress fewer than the NFL maximum of 48 players, even after practice-squad elevations. The 49ers expect to activate veteran receiver Christian Kirk, who has been on injured reserve with a calf injury since training camp, for his San Francisco debut. Evans’ Achilles tendinitis flared during the team’s Monday win over Washington, while Bosa remains out with a calf injury. San Francisco has a Week 8 bye before its Nov. 8 home game against Las Vegas.

sports.content: Former Napoli manager Antonio Conte said on Oct. 23 that he is not in advanced negotiations with any club, rejecting reports that he had discussed replacing Manchester United manager Michael Carrick after United’s 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como. Italian newspaper La Repubblica had reported that talks had taken place and that Conte wanted control of transfer policy and the right to appoint his own staff. Conte said those accounts were unfounded. United have begun identifying possible replacements, according to BBC Sport, but Carrick is set to remain in charge for the Premier League match against Bournemouth on Sunday, Oct. 25. The BBC said Conte is keen on the United job, while Conte said he would discuss a contract only if a concrete opportunity arose.

sports.summary: Paris Saint-Germain’s Ligue 1 match against Lyon has been moved from Sunday, October 25, to Monday, October 26, at 8:30 p.m. local time after Paris police barred it from going ahead on the original date. The teams entered the weekend level at the top of the table on 14 points. The rescheduled match falls on the same ev
sports.content: Paris Saint-Germain’s Ligue 1 match against Lyon has been moved from Sunday, October 25, to Monday, October 26, at 8:30 p.m. local time after Paris police barred it from going ahead on the original date. The teams entered the weekend level at the top of the table on 14 points. The rescheduled match falls on the same evening as the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London. Police requested the change because demonstrations were planned across France after violence and looting accompanied protests the previous weekend. Authorities also had to plan a large security deployment for Sunday’s NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France, north of central Paris. The French league accepted the police order and rescheduled the match; the NFL game remains scheduled for Sunday, October 25. The new timing may prevent PSG players who are fit to play and selected for the match from attending the London awards ceremony.

sports.title: Bayern coach Vincent Kompany hospitalized after collapsing during training
sports.summary: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital on Friday, Oct. 23, after collapsing while watching the club’s reserve team train. The 40-year-old is undergoing examinations and will remain under medical care, Bayern said; his coaching staff will oversee first-team training and matches in his absence. Ko
sports.content: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital on Friday, Oct. 23, after collapsing while watching the club’s reserve team train. The 40-year-old is undergoing examinations and will remain under medical care, Bayern said; his coaching staff will oversee first-team training and matches in his absence. Kompany had been ill with a virus in the days before the incident. He missed training and a pre-match news conference on Tuesday, but returned to the touchline for Bayern’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Arsenal on Wednesday. After that match, he said he had tried to work through the illness and ignored his body’s warning signs. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said Kompany would receive the care and time he needs to recover. The club is due to play Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday, Oct. 25; Kompany’s availability for the match has not been confirmed, and his assistants will manage the team until further notice.

sports.title: Poulter and Hatton quit LIV as three more players exit

sports.content: Ian Poulter and Tyrrell Hatton have joined three other players in rejecting LIV Golf’s planned 2027 relaunch after the league lost Saudi backing and filed for bankruptcy protection. Branden Grace, Tom McKibbin and Lucas Herbert have also said they are leaving. LIV is seeking to continue as “LIV 2.0” with a proposed $300 million financing package from BC Partners Credit after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund withdrew its support in April, having invested more than $5 billion. The league’s bankruptcy restructuring cancelled its existing player contracts, and only a handful of players have publicly committed to the proposed new circuit so far. Players face a reported Oct. 25 deadline to decide whether to sign on. The DP World Tour has said players who join LIV 2.0 will be ineligible for its 2027 membership, which is required for European Ryder Cup selection. LIV’s next bankruptcy hearing is scheduled for Nov. 5.
